newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Kosovo opposition condemns police killings.
newsitem.headline: Kosovo opposition condemns police killings.

text.p: A suspected commander of the outlawed Liberation Army of Kosovo was among three men killed in a gunbattle with Serbian police, the official Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported on Saturday.

A statement later faxed to Reuters in the Serbian capital by Kosovo's main ethnic Albanian political party condemned Friday's incident, saying it was part of a terror campaign by Serbian authorities against the region's majority Albanians.
Quoting the Serbian interior ministry, Tanjug said three police officers were wounded when they tried to stop a car carrying three men near the town of Vucitrn on Friday.
The agency identified the guerrilla suspect as 34-year-old Zahir Pajaziti. Police were shot at and returned fire, it said.

But the Democratic League, Kosovo's biggest ethnic Albanian party, said it condemned the killings, and in describing the incident it made no mention of any political or guerrilla affiliation of the three ethnic Albanians who died.

It cited witnesses as hearing shooting and finding spent cartridges, pools of blood and shattered glass at the scene. It named two of the victims as Hakif Zejnullahu, 34, and his uncle, Zahir Pajaziti. It said the third man had not yet been identified.

The League said its leadership "condemned in the strongest terms the killing yesterday of three Albanians in the midst of a huge crackdown". It urged the international community to persuade Belgrade to end its "campaign of terror".

In 1989 Serbia's autocratic President Slobodan Milosevic removed Albania's autonomous status, accusing the Albanian majority of preparing to secede. Ever since the province has been widely seen as a communal powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.

Friday's shooting follows what the League says has been a week-long series of heavy-handed Serbian police raids on ethnic Albanians' homes on the pretext of searching for guerrilla arms. It says there have been at least 37 arrests.

Mainstream Kosovo politicians have stayed well clear of marathon Serbian student and oppsosition protests against Milosevic for fear of becoming a convenient scapegoat for the increasingly beleaguered Belgrade government.
The clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army is reported to have been behind several guerrilla attacks over the past year in which both ethnic Albanians and Serbians have died.
